name: Saxon Hotel, Villas & Spa
positioning: Garden hotel on ten acres of indigenous gardens in Johannesburg's Sandhurst suburb, with suites in the main hotel and in private villas
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet garden setting in Johannesburg
Guests interested in Nelson Mandela's connection to the hotel

facts.text: The Saxon is in the tree-lined Johannesburg suburb of Sandhurst.
The Saxon is set on ten acres of indigenous gardens.
The property became a hotel in 2000.
Guests can stay in suites in the main hotel or in the more private Villa suites.
The Saxon Villas are in the gardens next to the hotel.
The villas can be booked as individual rooms or as entire units.
The Presidential Suites are decorated in a contemporary African style with stone cladding and light and dark woods.
Open-plan bathrooms have dual vanities, soaking tubs and separate showers.
Qunu, the main restaurant, overlooks the pool and gardens from indoor and outdoor dining spaces.
The Piano Lounge serves breakfast, al fresco dining, and morning and afternoon tea.
The kitchen uses ingredients hand-picked from the hotel's own herb and vegetable garden.
The wine cellars can host small private dinner parties.

highlights.text: Nelson Mandela wrote his autobiography at the Saxon.
The Nelson Mandela Platinum Suite is entered via a glass-enclosed elevator.
Qunu was awarded One Star by the EatOut Awards 2026.
The Saxon Spa uses the healing influences of copper and Himalayan salts.
The Terrace is a sundowner spot with views of the gardens and the infinity pool.

considerations.text: Sandhurst is an area of residences and quiet streets away from the center of busy Sandton.
Children are not a focus at the hotel, though families will be happy there.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the hotel's ultra-luxury positioning.
